question: A synthesis agent is producing a final report that combines a subagent's stock price and revenue trend findings with a subagent's qualitative summary of recent news coverage about the same company. Both are converted into the same bulleted list format in the draft report. What change would most improve how this content is rendered?
options: A) Convert the financial figures into prose paragraphs so they read alongside the news coverage without a jarring format change
B) Render the financial figures as a table and keep the news coverage as prose, matching each content type to its natural format
C) Combine the figures and news coverage into a single bulleted list that interleaves numbers and narrative sentences item by item
D) Convert the news coverage into the same bulleted list format as the financial figures so the whole report has one consistent style
correct_answers: B) Render the financial figures as a table and keep the news coverage as prose, matching each content type to its natural format
explanations: Converting tabular financial data into prose paragraphs makes it harder to scan and compare figures than a table would.

Correct. Financial data is best rendered as a table for easy comparison, while news content reads more naturally as prose; matching format to content type preserves clarity instead of flattening everything into one uniform shape.
Interleaving numeric data and narrative sentences in one list mixes formats that serve different purposes and makes both harder to read.
Forcing narrative news coverage into a bulleted list strips out the connective context and nuance that prose naturally conveys.
